site.title: Brand Identity | Pantalytics
site.description: Official brand identity and style guide for Pantalytics. Logo, colors, typography and tone of voice guidelines.
overview.title: Brand Identity — Pantalytics
overview.intro: This brand guide defines how Pantalytics presents itself visually and verbally. It is the single source of truth for logo usage, colors, typography and tone of voice.
overview.mission.title: Mission
overview.mission: Bring order to your business processes with secure, open source software.
overview.values.title: Brand values
overview.value.reliable.desc: European, GDPR-compliant, secure. We choose open source and avoid vendor lock-in.
overview.value.open.desc: Open source, transparent, no hidden costs or dependencies.
overview.value.practical.desc: Business-first, no-nonsense, results-driven. We solve real problems.
overview.value.smart.desc: AI-powered, data-informed, efficient. We automate what can be automated.
overview.audience.title: Who is this guide for?
overview.audience: Employees, partners, designers and agencies communicating on behalf of Pantalytics. Use these guidelines for presentations, websites, social media and all other communications.
overview.opensource.title: Open source
overview.opensource: This brand guide is open source. The code is MIT-licensed, the brand assets are CC BY-ND 4.0.
logo.title: Logo — Pantalytics
logo.intro: The Pantalytics logo is our primary identifier. Use it consistently and in accordance with the guidelines below.
logo.variants.title: Logo variants
logo.variants.desc: The Pantalytics logo is available in two versions: blue (primary) and gold (variant). An icon mark is also available for compact applications.
logo.primary.title: Primary logo (blue)
logo.primary.desc: The blue logo is the default version for all applications.
logo.gold.title: Gold variant
logo.gold.desc: The gold logo is an alternative for special applications, such as invitations or premium materials.
logo.icon.title: Icon mark
logo.icon.desc: The icon mark (circular emblem) is used as favicon, social media avatar and in compact spaces where the full logo doesn't fit.
logo.clearspace.title: Clear space
logo.clearspace: Maintain a minimum clear space equal to the height of the 'P' icon around the logo. This ensures the logo always has sufficient breathing room.
logo.minsize.title: Minimum size
logo.minsize: Do not use the logo smaller than 120px wide for digital applications or 30mm for print.
logo.dos.title: Do
logo.dos.1: Use the logo on approved backgrounds
logo.donts.title: Don't
logo.donts.4: Place the logo on busy backgrounds
colors.title: Colors — Pantalytics
colors.intro: The Pantalytics color palette is built around a dark, professional base with a recognizable purple accent. Use these colors consistently across all communications.
colors.logo.title: Logo colors
colors.logo.desc: The primary Pantalytics logo is navy blue. The gold variant is available for special applications.
colors.primary.title: Primary colors
colors.neutral.title: Text & background
colors.border.title: Borders
colors.contrast.title: WCAG Contrast ratios
colors.contrast.desc: The table below shows contrast ratios for commonly used combinations. Ensure text always meets the WCAG AA standard.
colors.modes.title: Dark mode & Light mode
colors.modes.desc: The Pantalytics color palette has two variants for app development. Dark mode is the primary brand environment; light mode is the lighter variant for everyday use.
colors.dark.title: Dark mode
colors.dark.desc: The default brand environment. Dark teal background with white and accent purple.
colors.light.title: Light mode
colors.light.desc: Light variant for apps and interfaces. The accent is darker (#5b58d8) to meet WCAG AA on white backgrounds.
colors.contrast.light.title: WCAG Contrast ratios — Light mode
colors.contrast.light.desc: Contrast ratios for the light mode color combinations.
colors.guidelines.title: Usage guidelines
colors.guideline.1: Never use accent purple (#9b99ff) as body text on a white background — the contrast is insufficient (3.02:1).
colors.guideline.2: The accent color is intended for interactive elements, eyebrows and decorative highlights.
colors.guideline.3: Dark teal backgrounds are the primary brand environment.
colors.guideline.4: White sections are used sparingly for emphasis and contrast.
typography.title: Typography — Pantalytics
typography.intro: Pantalytics uses two carefully chosen typefaces: Lexend for headings and Instrument Sans for body text. Both are self-hosted for GDPR compliance.
typography.heading.title: Lexend — Headings
typography.heading.desc: Lexend is used for all headings (h1–h6), logo text and statistics. Weight 500 (Medium) only.
typography.body.title: Instrument Sans — Body
typography.body.desc: Instrument Sans is used for body text, navigation, buttons and captions. Weights 400 (Regular), 500 (Medium) and 700 (Bold).
typography.scale.title: Type scale
typography.scale.desc: The type scale is based on a modular ratio and adapts across different screen sizes.
typography.rules.title: Rules
typography.rule.1: Headings are always Lexend 500 — never use bold (700) for headings.
typography.rule.2: Body text uses Instrument Sans 400 by default, 500 for medium emphasis (buttons, navigation), 700 for strong emphasis.
typography.rule.3: Eyebrow text (h6) is always uppercase with 0.1em letter-spacing in the accent color.
typography.rule.4: Do not use any other typefaces in Pantalytics materials.
typography.rule.5: For documents without self-hosted fonts (email, plain documents): use the system sans-serif stack as fallback.
typography.body.sample: We help companies streamline their processes with reliable, open source software. From CRM to invoicing, from inventory to project management — everything in one platform.
voice.title: Tone of Voice — Pantalytics
voice.intro: How Pantalytics communicates is just as important as how we look. Our voice is professional, clear and human.
voice.personality.title: Brand personality
voice.personality.professional.desc: We communicate clearly and directly. No jargon, no hype.
voice.personality.practical.desc: We focus on concrete outcomes, not abstract promises.
voice.personality.human.desc: We speak as entrepreneurs to entrepreneurs. First person plural ('we'), direct address ('you').
voice.personality.honest.desc: We give honest advice, even if it means recommending something else.
voice.attributes.title: Voice attributes
voice.dos.title: Writing guidelines
voice.do.1: Use active voice: 'We implement Odoo' not 'Odoo is implemented by us'.
voice.do.2: Be specific: '20-40% less effort' not 'significantly better results'.
voice.do.4: Lead with the customer benefit, not the technical feature.
voice.do.5: Keep sentences short. One idea per sentence.
voice.donts.title: Avoid
voice.dont.4: Overly formal language when a simple word works.
voice.dont.5: Unnecessary capitalization (e.g., 'Smart Business Software' only in titles).
voice.structure.title: Structure — Pyramid Principle
voice.structure.desc: All Pantalytics communication follows the McKinsey writing style: lead with the conclusion, then build your argument. The reader should be able to stop at any point and still understand the core message.
voice.pyramid.title: Pyramid structure
voice.pyramid.governing: Governing thought — One main message, as a complete sentence. This is the first thing the reader sees.
voice.pyramid.keyline: Key line — 2 to 5 supporting arguments. MECE: no overlap, no gaps.
voice.pyramid.evidence: Evidence — Data, examples, and substantiation per argument.
voice.pyramid.sowhat: 'So what?' test — Every point must survive this question. No answer? Cut it.
voice.scqa.title: SCQA for introductions
voice.scqa.s: Situation — Undisputed context the reader recognizes.
voice.scqa.q: Question — The implied question that follows.
voice.scqa.a: Answer — Your recommendation or conclusion, direct and clear.
voice.structure.slides.desc: Each slide or paragraph carries one message. The title is a complete sentence containing the insight — not a topic label.
voice.examples.title: Examples
voice.example.before.label: Don't
voice.example.after.label: Do
voice.example.1.before: Our state-of-the-art solutions facilitate your digital transformation.
voice.example.1.after: We help you streamline business processes with open source software.
voice.example.2.before: Our cutting-edge AI platform leverages synergies to drive digital transformation.
voice.example.2.after: Our AI reads Odoo source code, maps your data automatically, and tests continuously. You go live faster.
design.title: Design Philosophy — Pantalytics
design.intro: Our design principles guide every visual and interaction decision. From UI design to video production — these five principles form the foundation.
design.principles.title: Principles
design.principle.disclosure.title: Progressive Disclosure
design.principle.disclosure.desc: Show only what's needed, reveal complexity on demand. Users see the result first, then the details. Every additional option is a deliberate choice, not a default.
design.principle.disclosure.example: A dashboard shows three KPIs. Click a number, and the breakdown appears. Not the other way around.
design.principle.simplicity.title: Simplicity First
design.principle.simplicity.desc: Inspired by Vercel and Linear: clean, minimal, purposeful. Every element earns its place. If something can be removed without losing function, remove it.
design.principle.simplicity.example: No breadcrumbs when navigation is clear. No 'Are you sure?' dialog when undo is available.
design.principle.odoo.title: Odoo-Native Where Possible
design.principle.odoo.desc: We respect Odoo's conventions and framework. We don't add custom CSS where standard Odoo widgets suffice. But we do elevate the aesthetics where possible without breaking upgrade compatibility.
design.principle.odoo.example: Use Odoo's standard list/kanban views, but with optimized field order and smarter defaults.
design.principle.accessible.title: Accessible by Default
design.principle.accessible.desc: WCAG AA is the minimum, not the goal. Good contrast ratios, clear focus states, readable font sizes. Accessibility isn't a feature — it's the baseline.
design.principle.accessible.example: Accent purple becomes darker in light mode (#5b58d8 instead of #9b99ff) to ensure contrast.
design.principle.content.title: Content Over Chrome
design.principle.content.desc: UI serves the content, not the other way around. Data, text, and results take center stage. Decoration is secondary. An interface is good when the user forgets the interface.
design.principle.content.example: Reports show numbers large and clear. Navigation, filters, and actions are available but visually restrained.
design.visual.title: Visual Identity
design.visual.desc: Technology makes our lives better. Our visual language shows a world where AI and automation free people to do what makes them happy: being outdoors, social connection, nature, music, art, exercise. Technology is the enabler, not the subject.
design.visual.vision.title: Vision
design.visual.vision.desc: Most people spend their days behind screens, in offices, in factories, on the road. That is not what makes people happy. Pantalytics believes that AI — combined with European core values like democracy, freedom and human connection — can change this. Our visuals show that future: realistic yet absurdist, hopeful and inviting.
design.visual.style.title: Style: realistic absurdism
design.visual.style.desc: Photorealistic scenes with an absurdist twist. Technology — friendly robots, drones, AI companions — appears as a natural part of everyday life. Not as sci-fi, but as a better version of today.
design.visual.principles.title: Image principles
design.visual.principle.1: People first — laughing, relaxed, outdoors, connected
design.visual.principle.2: Technology as friend — robots are soft, organic, with warm navy blue (#1b3a5c) accents and friendly eyes
design.visual.principle.3: Always outdoors — nature, parks, beaches, mountains, European cities and landscapes
design.visual.principle.4: Bright and optimistic — sunlight, golden hour, blue skies, vivid colors
design.visual.principle.5: Absurdist twist — a dog sled pulled by robots, a humanoid waving a palm leaf, a drone delivering flowers
design.visual.principle.6: Navy blue (#1b3a5c) as consistent brand color on all technology
design.visual.tech.title: Technology in visuals
design.visual.tech.desc: Robots and AI companions are friendly, with soft rounded shapes that blend into their surroundings. They feel like trusted companions, not machines.
design.visual.tech.1: Quadruped robots — organic, soft, move like loyal dogs. Navy blue with warm eyes.
design.visual.tech.2: Humanoids — soft facial features, approachable, moves naturally. Navy blue accents.
design.visual.tech.3: Drones — rounded, organic design, navy blue with soft lights.
design.visual.tech.4: AI interfaces — subtly present, purple (#9b99ff) on digital screens, never dominant.
design.visual.scenes.title: Scene types
design.visual.scene.1: Adventure — robots joining hikes, surfing, cycling, sledding
design.visual.scene.2: Social — technology enabling a party, picnic or terrace gathering
design.visual.scene.3: Care — companions helping in the garden, reading aloud, bringing coffee
design.visual.scene.4: Freedom — humans are outdoors while AI handles the office work
design.visual.donts.title: Avoid
design.visual.dont.1: Cold, sterile technology imagery (white labs, blue neon glow)
design.visual.dont.2: People behind screens or in offices
design.visual.dont.5: Technology as subject instead of as enabler
design.visual.tone.title: Tone
design.visual.tone.desc: Bright, hopeful and warm. The world we show is a better version of today — not science fiction, not utopian, but realistically optimistic. As if you see a photo from next year and think: 'Yes, that's how I want to live.'
design.visual.color.title: Color in visuals
design.visual.color.desc: Navy blue (#1b3a5c) is the consistent brand color on all technology: robot accents, drone panels, companion details. Purple (#9b99ff) appears in digital interfaces and subtle light accents. Otherwise, natural colors dominate: green, sunlight gold, sky blue, sand.
design.systemprompt.title: AI System Prompt
design.systemprompt.desc: Give this text to any AI tool (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) as context when creating content or visuals for Pantalytics. Copy it in full.
design.fluxpreset.title: Flux Preset
design.fluxpreset.desc: Paste this preset before every Flux prompt. It contains the consistent brand style. Then add your specific scene.
design.visual.prompts.title: Flux Prompt Examples
design.visual.prompts.desc: Example prompts for specific scenes. Combine the preset above with one of these scenes.
design.photography.title: Photography
design.photography.desc: Guidelines for when real photography is used (team, events, office).
design.photography.prefer.title: Prefer
design.photography.prefer.3: Calm, clean compositions with generous negative space
design.photography.avoid.title: Avoid
design.photography.avoid.2: Flash lighting, bright colors, busy backgrounds
design.photography.avoid.4: Stock photos with visible watermarks or low resolution
design.photography.treatment.title: Color treatment
design.photography.treatment.desc: Slightly desaturate and shift white balance toward warm. Optionally apply a subtle teal overlay (10–15% opacity). The result should feel like natural daylight, not a filter.
design.charts.title: Data & Charts — Economist Style
design.charts.desc: Our charts and data visualizations follow The Economist style: clear, minimal, and conclusion-first.
design.charts.rules.title: Rules
design.charts.rule.1.title: Conclusion in the title
design.charts.rule.1.desc: The chart title is a complete sentence containing the insight. The subtitle provides context (unit, period).
design.charts.rule.1.good: 'MRR grew 34% after launching the self-service module'
design.charts.rule.2.title: Labels in the chart
design.charts.rule.2.desc: Label lines and bars directly in the chart. No separate legend box — this reduces eye travel.
design.charts.rule.3.title: One highlight color
design.charts.rule.3.desc: Use grey/muted tones as the base. Apply the accent color (#9b99ff dark / #5b58d8 light) to the key data series.
design.charts.rule.4.title: Minimal decoration
design.charts.rule.4.desc: No 3D effects, no chart junk. Light horizontal gridlines only, no vertical. No heavy borders or frames.
design.charts.rule.5.title: Y-axis starts at zero
design.charts.rule.5.desc: Bar charts always start at zero. Line charts may break this rule when variation matters more than absolute level, but this must be explicitly noted.
design.charts.rule.6.title: Source attribution
design.charts.rule.6.desc: Small text below the chart: 'Source: [provider]'. Always attribute, never omit.
design.templates.title: Templates & Formats
design.templates.desc: Standard formats for all content we produce. Use these dimensions and safe zones for consistent output.
design.templates.social.title: Social Media
design.templates.video.title: Video (Remotion)
design.templates.blog.title: Blog & Website
toolkit.title: Toolkit — Pantalytics
toolkit.intro: The open-source tools we use to produce all Pantalytics visuals, video and design. Everything runs locally, no vendor lock-in.
toolkit.flux.title: Flux
toolkit.flux.desc: Open-source image generation model. We use Flux via API to generate illustrations, social media visuals and concept images. Consistent brand style through LoRAs trained on our color palette.
toolkit.flux.usage: Social media visuals, blog hero images, concept illustrations, backgrounds
toolkit.penpot.title: Penpot
toolkit.penpot.desc: Open-source design platform as an alternative to Figma. We use Penpot for designing logo variants, social media templates, presentations and all design deliverables.
toolkit.penpot.usage: Logo variants, templates, presentations, UI design
toolkit.remotion.title: Remotion
toolkit.remotion.desc: React-based framework for creating videos programmatically. Ideal for automated video output such as intros, outros, social clips and data-driven animations.
toolkit.remotion.usage: Video intros/outros, social clips, lower thirds, data animations
toolkit.pixabay.title: Pixabay
toolkit.pixabay.desc: Royalty-free audio platform for background music, jingles and sound effects. All audio is free to use without attribution.
toolkit.pixabay.usage: Background music, jingles, sound effects for videos
toolkit.claude.title: Claude Code
toolkit.claude.desc: AI assistant for generating infographics, charts and data visualizations as SVG or HTML. Output is exported to PNG or SVG for use in presentations and publications.
toolkit.principle.title: Principle: open source first
toolkit.principle.desc: We consistently choose open-source tools. This aligns with our brand value 'Open': transparent, no hidden costs, no vendor lock-in. Only where no equivalent open-source alternative exists do we use commercial solutions.
